security_spec.violation_condition: When menvcfg.SSE is cleared to 0, the hardware does not force henvcfg.SSE to read-only zero via cascading override (`when(!menvcfg.SSE) { regOut.SSE := 0.U }`); a previously written non-zero henvcfg.SSE persists. Furthermore, senvcfg.SSE has no environment-bundle trait mixed in (no HasHypervisorEnvBundle or HasVirtualSupervisorEnvBundle), so it has zero cascading wiring from either menvcfg or henvcfg. Per the spec's simplified VU-mode check (only senvcfg.SSE tested, no longer also henvcfg.SSE), a stale senvcfg.SSE=1 directly grants spurious SSP access in VU-mode, bypassing the hypervisor's intent to disable shadow stacks.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: class HEnvCfg extends EnvCfg: SSE remains RO() but even if promoted to RW, no when(!menvcfg.SSE) cascading override exists; class SEnvCfg extends EnvCfg: SSE remains RO() but module instantiation has no env-bundle trait, so menvcfg/henvcfg cascading signals never reach senvcfg regOut
security_spec.summary: Defense-in-depth loss: PR simplifies VU-mode SSP check to only senvcfg.SSE (redundant henvcfg.SSE check removed), but XiangShan SEnvCfg module has no cascading wiring from either menvcfg or henvcfg, so any non-zero senvcfg.SSE survives higher-level disable — VU-mode shadow-stack access escapes hypervisor control
